extDescription.message: Protects you from fake websites and password theft. Works on your computer – sends no data anywhere.

pwAlertExplain.message: Scammers build pages that look just like the real ones to steal passwords. The safest thing is to leave this page now.

pwConfirmNewAccount.message: If you are creating a new account here, choose a different password – never reuse your bank or e-mail password on other sites.

reuseAdvice.message: It is safer to have a different password for every site. If someone learns it on one site, they can't get into the others.

btnUnderstoodRemember.message: Got it, don't show again on this site

findMixedBody.message: The address $P1$ mixes letters from different alphabets. Forged sites often look like this. Check the address carefully before typing anything.

findInsecureBody.message: The connection to this page is not encrypted (no padlock next to the address). Someone on the same Wi-Fi could see your password. Don't log in here.

findBlocklistedBody.message: $P1$ is on the list of data-stealing sites, but it was unblocked. Don't enter passwords, card details or payment codes here.

warnLead.message: We stopped a page that is on a list of data-stealing websites.

srcOpenphish.message: Source: OpenPhish – international list of phishing sites

leftTitle.message: Good! The suspicious page is closed

leftNothingSent.message: If a password was typed on that page, change it right away – on the service's real website.

warnWhy1.message: Such pages pretend to be a bank, courier, shop or government office to steal passwords, card details or payment codes.

warnWhy2.message: Links to them often arrive by text message or e-mail, e.g. about a parcel fee or a blocked account.

warnWhy3.message: A real bank never asks for your password or code through a link in a message.

warnAlreadyTitle.message: Already entered data on this page?

warnAlreadyText.message: Stay calm – there are simple steps worth taking right now.

proceedSummary.message: I know what I'm doing – let me in anyway

proceedText.message: We don't recommend this. Only continue if you are absolutely sure the page is safe. The page stays unblocked only until you close the browser.

proceedAck.message: I understand this page may steal my data or money.

proceedError.message: Could not unblock the page. Please try again.

footerPrivacy.message: CyberGuard works on your computer. It never sends anyone information about the pages you visit or your passwords.

popupHelpBtn.message: A scammer may have my data – what now?

helpPageTitle.message: What to do after a scam – CyberGuard

helpTitle.message: A scammer may have my data – what now?

helpIntro.message: Stay calm. This can happen to anyone. Take the steps below right away – the sooner, the better.

helpBankTitle.message: Card, payment code or online banking details

helpBank1.message: Call your bank. The number is on the back of your payment card or in your banking app. Never call numbers from text messages or e-mails.

helpBank2.message: Ask them to block your card and your online banking access.

helpBank3.message: Check with the bank whether there are transfers or payments you did not make.

helpPasswordTitle.message: Password for e-mail, a shop or another site

helpPassword1.message: Change the password on the service's real website – ideally from another, trusted device.

helpPasswordSessions.message: Sign out of all devices – in your account settings (usually "Security" → "Sign out of all devices"). If a scammer took over your logged-in session, a new password alone is not enough – this cuts them off.

helpPassword2.message: If the same password works anywhere else, change it there too.

helpPassword3.message: Turn on two-step login (text message or app code) if the service offers it.

helpIdTitle.message: ID number, identity card details or a photo of a document

helpId1.message: In Poland: block your PESEL number in the mObywatel app or on gov.pl (search for: zastrzeż PESEL). It's free.

helpId2.message: Report the identity document as compromised at any bank branch (Dokumenty Zastrzeżone system) or at your local office.

helpRemoteTitle.message: Someone talked you into installing a program (e.g. AnyDesk, TeamViewer)

helpRemote1.message: Disconnect the computer from the internet and ask a trusted person to help remove the program. The scammer may be able to see and control your screen through it.

helpReport1.message: Report the page to CERT Polska:

helpReport2.message: In Poland, forward a suspicious text message free of charge to 8080.

helpReport3.message: If money is gone, also report it to the police (emergency number 112).

helpTalkTitle.message: Talk to someone close to you

helpTalk1.message: Scammers frighten and rush people so there is no time to think. There is nothing to be ashamed of – talking to someone you trust helps you go through these steps calmly.

helpCleanText.message: Removes history, cookies, cache and form data from the last hour.

helpCleanNote.message: Note: you will be logged out of some sites. This does NOT undo data that already reached the scammer and does not sign them out of your accounts – the steps above matter most.

helpCleanDone.message: Done. Data from the last hour has been removed.

helpCleanDenied.message: Data can't be cleared without the browser's permission.

helpCleanFailed.message: Could not clear the data. You can do it in the browser settings (Ctrl+Shift+Delete).

welcomeLead.message: There is nothing to set up. The extension works on its own:

welcome1.message: It stops known scam pages (CERT Polska and OpenPhish lists).

welcome2.message: It warns you when your bank, e-mail or government password is typed on a foreign site.

welcome3.message: It warns about pages pretending to be well-known companies.

welcomeNothingToDo.message: The shield icon next to the address bar tells you whether a page is known. You can close this tab now.

optFeedToggle.message: Download new CERT Polska warnings (every 12 hours)

optFeedPrivacy.message: The extension only downloads a public list. It never sends information about the pages you visit or about you.

optFeedError.message: The last attempt failed – we'll try again later.

optFeedBuilt.message: Protecting you from $P1$ dangerous pages (list from $P2$).

optFeedTotal.message: In total we protect you from $P1$ dangerous pages: $P2$ from the list built into the extension (from $P3$) and $P4$ new ones added by CERT Polska since then.

optFeedRemoved.message: $P1$ pages that CERT Polska withdrew from its list are no longer blocked.

optPasswordsText.message: CyberGuard does not store passwords. It keeps only a "fingerprint" that can't be turned back into the password, so it knows where each password is used.

optPasswordsEmpty.message: Nothing remembered yet. The list appears after your first login.

optForgetAllConfirm.message: Are you sure? Password protection will start learning from scratch.

optTrustedText.message: Sites where you clicked "I trust this site" or "Got it, don't show again". The warning about your bank or e-mail password always works, here too.

optAllowedTitle.message: Pages unblocked until the browser closes

optAllowedText.message: These pages are on the dangerous list but were unblocked. They will be blocked again when you close the browser.

optAbout1.message: CyberGuard checks everything on your computer. Passwords are never sent or stored anywhere.

optAbout2.message: Dangerous page lists: CERT Polska (hole.cert.pl) and OpenPhish.
